text: A role is granted to another role (GRANT ROLE junior TO ROLE senior). What does this create?

options.A: A copy of the junior role's privileges into senior
options.B: A role hierarchy — senior inherits all privileges held by junior
options.C: A shared ownership between both roles
options.D: A temporary delegation that expires after 24 hours

explanation: Granting a role to another role creates a hierarchy. The parent role inherits all privileges of the child role. This is how RBAC hierarchies work in Snowflake.

text: A user's DEFAULT_ROLE is set to ANALYST. They log in and run SHOW GRANTS TO USER. They see ANALYST, DATA_ENG, and PUBLIC. Can they access objects owned by DATA_ENG without switching roles?

options.A: No — only the default role is active at login
options.B: Yes — if USE SECONDARY ROLES ALL is enabled, all granted roles contribute privileges simultaneously
options.C: No — they must run USE ROLE DATA_ENG first
options.D: Yes — all granted roles are always active

explanation: With USE SECONDARY ROLES ALL, all granted roles are active alongside the primary. Without it, only the primary role (DEFAULT_ROLE or explicitly set role) determines privileges. The user must either switch roles or enable secondary roles.

text: OWNERSHIP on a schema is transferred to a new role using GRANT OWNERSHIP ... REVOKE CURRENT GRANTS. What happens to existing grants on objects inside the schema?

options.B: All existing grants on objects within that schema are REVOKED — REVOKE CURRENT GRANTS removes them during transfer
options.D: Grants are moved to the new owner automatically

explanation: REVOKE CURRENT GRANTS in an OWNERSHIP transfer statement revokes all existing grants on child objects. Use COPY CURRENT GRANTS to preserve them. This is a critical choice during ownership transfer.

text: What is the maximum number of key pairs a single user can have registered simultaneously?

options.B: 2 — RSA_PUBLIC_KEY and RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2 for zero-downtime rotation
options.D: Unlimited

explanation: Each user can have at most 2 active public keys: RSA_PUBLIC_KEY (primary) and RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2 (secondary for rotation). This allows updating clients without downtime.

text: A password policy requires passwords to be changed every 90 days. A user's password expires. Can they still log in?

options.A: Yes — expired passwords allow login but prompt an immediate change
options.B: No — the account is locked until an admin resets it
options.C: Yes — password policies are advisory only
options.D: No — the session is terminated after the last query

explanation: When a password expires under a password policy, the user can still authenticate but is immediately prompted to change their password before proceeding. The account is not locked.

text: A masking policy body contains: CASE WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN ('HR') THEN val ELSE '***' END. A user with secondary role HR but primary role ANALYST queries the column. What do they see?

options.A: The unmasked value because HR is active
options.B: '***' — because CURRENT_ROLE() only returns the PRIMARY role (ANALYST), which is not HR
options.D: An error

explanation: CURRENT_ROLE() returns only the primary role. Since primary = ANALYST (not HR), the CASE falls to ELSE. To check secondary roles, use IS_ROLE_IN_SESSION('HR') instead.

text: A row access policy is attached to table T1. A materialized view is created on T1 with a WHERE clause. Is the row access policy applied when querying the MV?

options.A: No — MVs pre-compute results and bypass policies
options.B: Yes — row access policies are enforced at query time regardless of the access path, including through MVs
options.C: Only if the MV is secure
options.D: Only for the first query after refresh

explanation: Row access policies are enforced at query time. Even though an MV pre-computes data, the policy is applied when the MV is queried. This prevents policy bypass through materialized views.

text: An engineer runs SYSTEM$CLASSIFY on a table and receives results categorizing columns with 'SEMANTIC_CATEGORY' and 'PRIVACY_CATEGORY'. What is the next step to actually PROTECT the classified columns?

options.B: Manually apply tags based on the classification results, then attach masking policies to those tags
options.D: No action needed — columns are encrypted after classification

explanation: SYSTEM$CLASSIFY only DETECTS and RECOMMENDS. It does not enforce anything. You must: (1) apply tags to columns based on results, (2) attach masking policies to those tags. Classification → Tagging → Policy = the enforcement chain.

text: What is the difference between ACCESS_HISTORY and QUERY_HISTORY in ACCOUNT_USAGE?

options.B: QUERY_HISTORY tracks query execution details. ACCESS_HISTORY tracks which data COLUMNS were read or written.
options.C: ACCESS_HISTORY is real-time; QUERY_HISTORY has latency
options.D: QUERY_HISTORY only shows failed queries

explanation: QUERY_HISTORY: execution metadata (duration, warehouse, user, SQL text). ACCESS_HISTORY: column-level data lineage (which columns were accessed, direct vs base objects). Different purposes — execution vs data access auditing.

text: A resource monitor at the warehouse level suspends WH_A. Can users submit queries to a different warehouse WH_B?

options.A: No — resource monitors suspend all warehouses in the account
options.B: Yes — warehouse-level monitors only affect the specific warehouse they are assigned to
options.C: Only if WH_B has no monitor
options.D: Only ACCOUNTADMIN can submit to WH_B

explanation: Warehouse-level resource monitors only affect the specific warehouse(s) they are assigned to. Other warehouses continue operating normally, even if they share the same account.

text: An engineer needs query history from 400 days ago. Where can they find it?

options.B: Nowhere — ACCOUNT_USAGE retains for 365 days only; data older than that is purged
options.D: The Snowsight Activity tab stores unlimited history

explanation: ACCOUNT_USAGE views retain data for 365 days maximum. Data older than 365 days is purged permanently. INFORMATION_SCHEMA retains only 7-14 days. There is no built-in mechanism to query beyond 365 days.

text: Network policy evaluation order: account-level policy allows 10.0.0.0/8. User-level policy has ALLOWED_IP_LIST empty but BLOCKED_IP_LIST = ('10.5.5.5/32'). User connects from 10.1.1.1. What happens?

options.A: Blocked — user policy takes effect and has no allowed IPs
options.B: Allowed — account policy applies because user policy has empty allowed list
options.C: Allowed — user-level overrides, and with empty ALLOWED = allow all EXCEPT blocked IPs
options.D: Error — empty allowed list is invalid

explanation: User-level policy overrides account. An empty ALLOWED_IP_LIST means ALL IPs are allowed (no restriction). BLOCKED_IP_LIST then blocks specific IPs. So 10.1.1.1 is allowed (not in blocked list), but 10.5.5.5 would be blocked.

text: What does GRANT MANAGE GRANTS ON ACCOUNT TO ROLE my_role enable?

options.B: The ability to grant or revoke ANY privilege on ANY object in the account — equivalent to SECURITYADMIN's core power
options.D: Only creating new roles

explanation: MANAGE GRANTS is the global privilege that allows granting/revoking any privilege on any object. This is what makes SECURITYADMIN powerful. Granting it to a custom role effectively gives it SECURITYADMIN-level access control authority.

text: An object tag hierarchy exists: tag on DATABASE → propagates to SCHEMA → propagates to TABLE → propagates to COLUMN. At which level does a tag-based masking policy actually mask data?

options.B: At the COLUMN level — tag-based masking only activates on columns whose data type matches the policy signature, regardless of where the tag was applied
options.D: Only at the table level

explanation: Tag-based masking policies are evaluated at the column level during query execution. Even if the tag was applied at a higher level (table/schema/database) and propagated down, masking only occurs for columns whose data type matches the policy signature.

text: Which ACCOUNT_USAGE view shows storage broken down by active data, Time Travel data, and Fail-safe data for each table?

options.B: TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS
options.D: DATA_TRANSFER_HISTORY

explanation: TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS provides ACTIVE_BYTES, TIME_TRAVEL_BYTES, and FAILSAFE_BYTES for each table. This enables identifying tables with disproportionate CDP storage costs.

text: Which TWO system functions help determine active roles in a session? (Select TWO)

options.A: CURRENT_ROLE() — returns the primary role only
options.B: IS_ROLE_IN_SESSION() — checks if a specific role is active (primary or secondary)
options.C: SHOW GRANTS — lists all account grants
options.D: CURRENT_USER() — returns the username

explanation: CURRENT_ROLE() returns the primary active role. IS_ROLE_IN_SESSION(role) checks whether a specific role is anywhere in the active hierarchy (including secondary roles). These serve different purposes in policy logic.

text: An engineer creates an alert: CREATE ALERT ... WAREHOUSE=wh1 SCHEDULE='USING CRON ...' IF(EXISTS(SELECT ...)) THEN CALL system$send_email(...). What determines whether the alert fires?

options.A: The alert fires every time the schedule triggers
options.B: Only when the SQL condition returns at least ONE row at the scheduled check time
options.D: When any user queries the monitored table

explanation: Alerts evaluate their SQL condition on schedule. The action (THEN clause) only fires when the condition returns one or more rows. If zero rows are returned, nothing happens until the next scheduled check.

text: What minimum privilege is needed to see the definition (DDL) of a view you don't own?

options.B: No additional privilege — anyone with USAGE can see the definition unless the view is SECURE
options.D: REFERENCES on the view

explanation: For standard (non-secure) views, any user with USAGE on the containing schema can see the view definition via GET_DDL or SHOW VIEWS. Secure views hide their definition from all non-owners.

text: Data in transit between a client and Snowflake is encrypted using what protocol?

options.B: TLS 1.2 or higher
options.D: AES-256 file encryption

explanation: All data in transit (client ↔ Snowflake, Snowflake ↔ cloud storage) uses TLS 1.2 minimum. AES-256 is for data at rest. SSH and IPSec are not used.

text: An account-level resource monitor is set with credit_quota=1000 and frequency=MONTHLY. On day 15, consumption reaches 1000. What happens at the start of next month?

options.A: The quota remains exhausted until manually reset
options.B: The quota automatically RESETS to 1000 at the start of the new frequency period (monthly)
options.D: The monitor is automatically dropped

explanation: Resource monitor quotas reset automatically at the start of each frequency period (DAILY/WEEKLY/MONTHLY/YEARLY). At month start, the 1000-credit quota resets and tracking begins fresh.
